# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).

    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

args.question: I'm way behind on pieces (20 vs 34) and there's only 10 empty spaces left on the board. I have to pick from g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, or c8. Which one gives me the best shot at catching up by the end? I don't really know how to think this through.

parts.content:
Best shot: **b7**.

The key feature is the **bottom-left corner area**: moves like **a7, b8, or c8** can make it easier for White to get or stabilize the **a8 corner/edge**, while **b7** keeps more control and doesn’t immediately hand over a corner. In endgames, you’re trying to maximize the **final count**, not the flips right now—**b7** leaves Black with the best end result from these legal choices.
Alright, b7 it is then. Let's give it a shot.

args.question: I ended up picking g2 near the end because it looked like it flipped a long line of pieces down that column, and I figured it'd work out even after White took the last corner spot. Was that actually the right call, or did I just get lucky it worked out to 33-31?

parts.content:
It wasn’t just luck — **g2 was a real endgame shot**, and in the actual line it worked: Black finished **33–31**.

The deciding feature was **final mobility/sequence**, not the long flip by itself: even though White got the corner afterward, Black still had enough follow-up flips/last moves to swing the final count. So your instinct happened to match the concrete endgame better than the general “avoid corner-adjacent squares” rule here.
